cards.name: Extract
cards.summary: Luminance (or single-channel) key: pixels darker than Black Point or brighter than White Point become transparent, with softness ramps at both ends. Keys out black or white backgrounds and can punch bright or dark areas out of footage.
use_for: remove a black or white background from stock smoke, sparks, ink or light-leak footage
pull a quick key off a white-backdrop product shot or a flat graphic/screenshot (not people: it also removes white shirts, teeth and eye highlights)
luminance wipe: animate White Point down so a press photo dissolves from its highlights
cut a scanned logo or signature off white paper for an explainer
avoid: on normal live-action it eats faces and shirts along with the background, leaving blotchy holes
hard Black/White Points with 0 softness give jagged, buzzing edges on compressed footage

params.name: Channel
params.does: what the key is based on (dropdown: luminance, a colour channel or alpha)

params.name: Black Point
params.does: pixels darker than this become transparent

params.name: White Point
params.does: pixels brighter than this become transparent
params.typical: 200-240 to drop a white background; 255 keeps all brights

params.name: Black Softness
params.does: feather of the dark cut-off

params.name: White Softness
params.does: feather of the bright cut-off

params.name: Invert
params.does: checkbox: makes the range BETWEEN Black Point and White Point transparent instead of the range outside it

cards.equivalent: Luma Key (Premiere; keys the dark range only) or Logo Cutout for a plain black/white background. NOT Premiere's 'Extract', which is a different effect (black-and-white threshold, no transparency)
cards.scripting: Values are 8-bit 0-255 levels even in 16/32 bpc projects. Keep White Point above Black Point. Invert is a 0/1 checkbox. Keyed areas show the comp background (black in our renders), so on an opaque comp it reads as black holes.

verified.note: Luma key is obvious: the white wall, white stripes and skin highlights (above White Point 170) and the darkest hair/shadows (below Black Point 40) go to black comp background, leaving the mid-tone clothing, red foreground blocks and stripes with soft fringed edges (mean luma 155 to 74).

cards.name: Inner/Outer Key
cards.summary: Isolates a subject with fuzzy edges (hair, fur, smoke) from two rough masks: one drawn inside the subject and one outside it; the effect computes the soft edge in between. Without masks on the layer it does nothing.
use_for: cut a person with flyaway hair off a busy, non-green background for a cutout collage
isolate a leader from a press photo to place over a new graphic background
extract smoke or foliage edges that a hard mask cannot follow
avoid: on moving footage the masks must be animated frame by frame; Roto Brush is usually faster
low-contrast edges (dark hair on dark background) come out patchy

params.name: Foreground (Inside)
params.does: mask on the same layer drawn just inside the subject
params.typical: mask index of the inner mask

params.name: Background (Outside)
params.does: mask drawn just outside the subject edge
params.typical: mask index of the outer mask

params.name: Single Mask Highlight Radius
params.does: edge band width when only one mask is supplied

params.name: Edge Thin
params.does: shrinks (+) or grows (-) the matte edge

params.name: Edge Feather
params.does: softens the matte edge

params.name: Edge Threshold
params.does: removes low-opacity noise from the edge

params.name: Blend with Original
params.does: mixes the original layer back over the result

cards.scripting: All Foreground/Background/Path params are mask-reference params (value = mask index on the same layer, 0 = none): they cannot be set from a spec; create masks with ExtendScript first and set the indices directly. Path, Brush Radius and Brush Pressure repeat for 8 foreground then 8 background cleanup strokes; the repeats are addressed as "Brush Radius#2" ... "Brush Radius#16" (ae_lib child() resolves Name#N). Edge Threshold and Blend with Original are raw 0-1 values.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs foreground/background masks drawn on the layer; mask-reference params cannot be set from a spec), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: needs_input/not_rendered agreed (every Foreground/Background/Path param is mask-type); scripting wrongly said only the first repeated cleanup param is reachable, Name#N addressing reaches all 16

cards.name: Key Cleaner
cards.summary: Repairs the alpha of an already keyed layer: restores fine edge detail (hair, motion blur) lost to the key and reduces matte chatter. On footage without a key (fully opaque) it shows no change.
use_for: after Keylight on a green-screen anchor or explainer host to recover hair edges
reduce boiling edges on a keyed presenter in a news package
clean a key on compressed (H.264) green-screen footage
avoid: it cannot rescue a bad key: fix the Keylight screen matte first
large Additional Edge Radius brings back spill and background fringe

params.name: Additional Edge Radius
params.does: how far from the matte edge detail is recovered

params.name: Reduce Chatter
params.does: checkbox: temporal smoothing of jittery edges

params.name: Alpha Contrast
params.does: hardens semi-transparent edge pixels

params.name: Strength
params.does: overall amount of the cleanup

cards.equivalent: Ultra Key's Matte Cleanup section (Premiere; cleans only Ultra Key's own key, no standalone key cleaner)
cards.scripting: Must be stacked AFTER the keying effect (Keylight) on the same layer; needs a real alpha to act on. Reduce Chatter is a 0/1 checkbox. No visible demo on opaque footage, hence needs_input.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an already keyed layer with real alpha; on the opaque photo it is a no-op), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Keylight (1.2)
cards.summary: Professional colour-difference keyer: removes a chosen screen colour (green or blue) and suppresses its spill on the foreground, with matte clipping, shrink/grow and edge colour controls. The standard tool for green-screen presenters.
use_for: key a green-screen anchor or explainer host over a news set or B-roll
drop a presenter into a reel background or animated graphics
key screens/phone inserts shot with green content
punch out a sky or backdrop colour for a stylised trailer composite
avoid: uneven, wrinkled or spill-heavy screens need Clip Black/White tuning plus Key Cleaner, not just one colour pick
on footage without a real screen it eats every pixel of that hue (blue suits, flags) and tints skin magenta
heavy Screen Pre-blur or Softness gives a glowy, cheap halo

params.name: Screen Colour
params.does: the background colour to remove
params.typical: the green/blue of the screen, e.g. #20B040

params.name: View
params.does: dropdown: what is displayed (Screen Matte to judge the key, Final Result to output)
params.typical: 11 for output, 5 to check the matte

params.name: Screen Gain
params.does: how aggressively the screen colour is removed

params.name: Screen Balance
params.does: balance between the other two channels when computing the key

params.name: Clip Black
params.does: pushes grey background areas of the matte to fully transparent

params.name: Clip White
params.does: pushes grey foreground areas of the matte to fully opaque

params.name: Screen Shrink/Grow
params.does: erodes (-) or expands (+) the matte edge

params.name: Screen Softness
params.does: blurs the matte edge

cards.scripting: Default Screen Colour is black, so nothing is keyed until Screen Colour is set ("#RRGGBB"). Many names repeat in this effect: Replace Method / Replace Colour (Screen Matte vs Inside Mask), Invert (Inside vs Outside Mask), Saturation, Contrast, Brightness, Suppress, Suppression Balance, Suppression Amount, Hue, Sat (Foreground vs Edge colour correction); our AE applier takes the FIRST property with a name, so the second copies need property-index access. Inside Mask / Outside Mask are mask-reference params (not settable from a spec). Group headers are flat rows, so use plain names, not Group/Name. Enum orders for View, Replace Method and Source Alpha follow the Keylight manual and match the harvested defaults (11, 4, 3); the Suppress order (1 None, 2 Red, 3 Green, 4 Blue, 5 Cyan, 6 Magenta, 7 Yellow) and X / Y Method (1 Colour, 2 Repeat, 3 Reflect, 4 Wrap) are read from After Effects 26.0, as are the others.

verified.note: Blue screen colour #1A4FBF keys the navy areas and a blue block to solid black while faces, red stripes, foreground blocks and flowers stay intact, and the cool-white wall is despilled slightly warmer: exactly the 'eats every pixel of that hue' case the card warns about.

cards.name: Linear Color Key
cards.summary: Simple colour key: removes (or keeps) pixels close to a chosen Key Color, matched by RGB, hue or chroma, with tolerance and softness. Quick and crude compared with Keylight.
use_for: quick key of a flat, evenly lit screen or solid graphic background
remove a single flat colour from a logo or chart screenshot
Keep Colors mode to isolate one colour (e.g. a party flag) for a stylised highlight
second pass on a Keylight key to remove a stubborn colour patch
avoid: on real green-screen footage edges are hard and spill stays; use Keylight
high tolerance on live action eats skin and clothing of similar hue

Match colors = Using Hue ignores saturation, so near-grey areas with a faint cool cast go too (on the demo it dropped the off-white wall along with the navy areas); use Using RGB or Chroma to spare neutrals

params.name: Key Color
params.does: colour to remove (or keep)

params.name: Match colors
params.does: dropdown: colour space used for matching

params.name: Matching Tolerance
params.does: how far a colour may be from Key Color and still be keyed

params.name: Matching Softness
params.does: feather of the tolerance edge

params.name: Key Operation
params.does: dropdown: remove the key colour or keep only it

params.name: View
params.does: dropdown: final output, source only or matte only

cards.scripting: Key Color takes "#RRGGBB". Stack a second Linear Color Key with Key Operation = 2 (Keep Colors) to protect a colour the first one removed. Tolerance/Softness are 0-100 percent.

verified.note: Hue-matched blue key removes the navy areas, a blue block and most of the cool grey-white wall and the left-hand colour block to black, keeping faces, red stripes, foreground blocks, flowers and plants; crude hard-edged blotches as the card says.

cards.name: Unmult
cards.summary: Turns brightness into transparency: a black background becomes transparent while bright elements keep their full colour (White mode does the reverse, removing a white background and keeping dark elements), so flares, fire, sparks and light leaks shot on black composite cleanly without a blend mode.
use_for: overlay stock light leaks, lens flares, dust or embers shot on black over footage
use fire/explosion elements in a trailer while keeping Normal blend mode (so they still work inside precomps and track mattes)
drop black-background motion graphics or particles over B-roll
remove a white background from ink or paper texture (Background Color = White)
avoid: on normal live action it makes dark areas see-through, so the shot looks washed out over anything but black
dense, opaque elements (thick smoke) lose body because dark interior pixels become transparent

params.name: Background Color
params.does: dropdown: which background is made transparent
params.typical: 1 (Black) for flares/fire; 2 (White) for ink on paper

params.name: Black Level
params.does: raises the level treated as background, cleaning noisy near-black areas

params.name: Softness
params.does: how gradually alpha ramps up from the background level

params.name: Remove Color Matting
params.does: checkbox: un-premultiplies colour so edges keep full colour

params.name: Clip HDR Results
params.does: checkbox: clamps over-range values in 32 bpc

cards.equivalent: none as such in Premiere; closest effect is Logo Cutout (keys a plain black/white background by brightness); for flares on black use the clip's Opacity > Blend Mode = Screen
cards.scripting: Built-in AE effect doing what the third-party Unmult plug-ins (Knoll / Red Giant) did, so no plug-in is needed; the AE version that introduced it is unverified. Over a black comp background, Background Color = Black looks almost unchanged by design (it only adds alpha); the demo uses White so the effect is visible. Background Color: 1 Black (default), 2 White (read from After Effects 26.0); Black Level/Softness units are unverified, keep near defaults.

verified.note: White mode turns brightness into transparency inverted: the white wall, stripes and highlights vanish and the whole frame falls to near black (mean luma 155 to 9.5), with only dim, saturated reds, blues and greens left where the image was dark or coloured.

cards.name: Matte Choker
cards.summary: Two-pass spread/choke of a layer's alpha with geometric and grey-level softness: fills small holes and tightens or softens the edges of a keyed or rotoscoped matte. Also used to merge shapes into gooey blobs.
use_for: tighten a green-screen key that has a fringe after Keylight
fill speckle holes in a luma/colour key
gooey/metaball merge of blurred shapes or text for a reel transition
soften harsh edges of a roto cutout before compositing
avoid: large choke values round off fingers, hair and text corners
on opaque full-frame footage it does nothing at all (verified: not even the frame border changes, unlike Simple Choker)

params.name: Geometric Softness 1
params.does: radius (px) of the first spread/choke pass

params.name: Choke 1
params.does: first pass: positive values choke (shrink) the matte, negative values spread it, which fills small holes
params.typical: 30-75 to tighten a fringe (default 75); -20 to -60 to fill holes, then choke back with a positive Choke 2

params.name: Gray Level Softness 1
params.does: how soft the resulting edge is (0 hard, 1 soft)

params.name: Geometric Softness 2
params.does: radius of the second pass

params.name: Choke 2
params.does: second pass choke (+) / spread (-), usually used to choke back after a spreading first pass

params.name: Iterations
params.does: repeats both passes

cards.equivalent: none as a standalone effect in Premiere; Ultra Key's Matte Cleanup > Choke only chokes Ultra Key's own key
cards.scripting: Gray Level Softness values are raw 0-1 (UI shows %). Acts only on the alpha produced by masks or effects above it, so stack it after the key. Verified on the opaque demo clip: zero change at full 1920x1080, frame edge included, hence needs_input. demo_settings are a moderate ~8 px choke for a source with real alpha; the 40 px / Choke 127 push used for the opaque test would erase text strokes and fingers on a real matte. Measured live wave 3: on a cut-out with a soft alpha edge the demo pulled the edge in and hardened it (a 24 px feather became about 8 px); after Keylight on a green-screen plate it also removed the fine semi-transparent strands and the screen residue.

verified.note: On the alpha cut-out the disc's soft edge is choked to a tighter, harder edge (24 px ramp to about 8 px, the disc slightly smaller) and after Keylight the strands and screen residue are gone: it tightens a matte, as the card says.

previous.why: the test footage has nothing for it to act on (see note), so the render could not show it doing its job
judged on the live wave 3 re-render on the second (synthetic) footage set, which has what the card acts on
previous.note: Frame is pixel-identical to the untouched render (zero difference, frame border not eroded either): Matte Choker treats the opaque full-frame layer as having no alpha edge to choke, so no demo value can show it; status set to needs_input (needs a keyed/rotoscoped layer, text or shapes with real alpha as the demo source).
previous.second_opinion: corrected: verdict agreed (full-res G133 render is pixel-identical to the no-op renders G051/G234, border included; Simple Choker 134 does erode the border); demo_settings 40/127/0.2 were a destructive ~40 px choke on any real matte, now 10/100/0.2 (top of the card's typical softness range, choke just above it so the demo stays visible); dropped the unverified 'treats outside-the-layer as opaque' claim and 'photo' -> clip

cards.name: Refine Hard Matte
cards.summary: Roto Brush-style edge refinement for a hard-edged matte: feathers, contrasts, shifts the edge, reduces chatter, adds motion blur and decontaminates edge colours. Needs a layer that already has an alpha matte (key, mask or track matte).
use_for: smooth the edge of a masked or keyed object (podium, phone, vehicle) before compositing
add matching motion blur to a fast-moving roto cutout in a trailer
remove background colour fringe from a cut-out press photo subject
avoid: for hair and fur use Refine Soft Matte instead
Use Motion Blur with many samples is slow on long clips

params.name: Feather
params.does: softens the matte edge

params.name: Contrast
params.does: hardens the feathered edge

params.name: Shift Edge
params.does: moves the edge in (-) or out (+)

params.name: Reduce Chatter
params.does: temporal smoothing of the edge

params.name: Use Motion Blur
params.does: checkbox: motion-blurs the matte edge

params.name: Decontaminate Edge Colors
params.does: checkbox: removes background colour from edge pixels

params.name: Amount
params.does: strength of edge-colour decontamination

params.name: View Map
params.does: checkbox: shows the decontamination map for checking

cards.scripting: Acts on the alpha produced by masks or effects above it; on opaque footage there is no visible change. Use Motion Blur, Higher Quality, Decontaminate Edge Colors, Extend Where Smoothed and View Map are 0/1 checkboxes. Samples Per Frame and Shutter Angle only matter when Use Motion Blur = 1.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a layer that already has an alpha matte; on the opaque photo it is a no-op), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Refine Soft Matte
cards.summary: Edge refinement for soft, detailed mattes (hair, fur, smoke): recalculates edge detail inside an edge band, then smooths, feathers, shifts and decontaminates it. Needs a layer that already has an alpha matte.
use_for: recover flyaway hair on a roto-brushed or keyed presenter
soften a cutout of a leader from a press photo for a parallax explainer
remove green/background fringe from soft edges
avoid: a wide Additional Edge Radius pulls background texture into the matte
heavier than Refine Hard Matte; avoid on long clips when a hard edge is fine

params.name: Additional Edge Radius
params.does: width of the band where edge detail is recalculated

params.name: Calculate Edge Details
params.does: checkbox: enables the detail recalculation

params.name: View Edge Region
params.does: checkbox: displays the edge band for checking

params.name: Smooth
params.does: smooths the matte edge

params.name: Feather
params.does: softens the edge

params.name: Shift Edge
params.does: moves the edge in (-) or out (+)

params.name: Reduce Chatter
params.does: temporal smoothing of edge jitter

params.name: Decontaminate Edge Colors
params.does: checkbox: removes background colour from edge pixels

cards.scripting: Acts on the alpha produced by masks or effects above it; on opaque footage there is no visible change. Chatter Reduction: 1 Off (default), 2 a separator, 3 More Detailed, 4 Smoother (Slower) (read from After Effects 26.0); Reduce Chatter is its amount. Checkboxes are 0/1.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a layer that already has an alpha matte; on the opaque photo it is a no-op), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Simple Choker
cards.summary: Shrinks (positive) or spreads (negative) a layer's alpha edge by a number of pixels. A one-slider fix for fringes on keys and a way to fatten or thin text and shapes.
use_for: remove a 1-2 px fringe from a green-screen key
animate text growing from thin to full weight in a reel title
fatten or thin a cut-out logo or shape layer
gooey merge after Fast Box Blur on shapes
avoid: large values round off corners and destroy thin strokes
on opaque full-frame footage it only eats into the frame border

params.name: Choke Matte
params.does: pixels to choke (+) or spread (-) the alpha edge
params.typical: 1-3 for keys; -5 to 20 for text animation

params.name: View
params.does: dropdown: final output or the matte

cards.equivalent: none as a standalone effect in Premiere; Ultra Key's Matte Cleanup > Choke only chokes Ultra Key's own key
cards.scripting: Stack after the key. Verified on the opaque demo frame: it treats outside-the-layer as transparent, so the visible result is an eroded black border with rounded corners around the frame edge, interior unchanged (Matte Choker, by contrast, shows nothing there). Set View = 2 to inspect the alpha.

verified.note: Choke Matte 80 eats a solid black border about 8 px wide (in the 640 px frame) around the opaque layer with clearly rounded corners, interior untouched: the eroded-alpha-edge behaviour the card describes, shown on the only alpha edge the photo has.

cards.name: Add Grain
cards.summary: Synthesises realistic film grain with control over intensity, size, softness, per-channel response, colour and animation, optionally from film-stock presets. Unifies CG, stock and phone footage into one filmic texture.
use_for: give documentary archival recreations a film look
match the grain of graphics and AI shots to camera footage in a trailer
texture a cinematic title card or end slate
monochrome grain on black-and-white flashback sequences
avoid: left in the default Preview viewing mode it renders grain only inside a boxed region with an outline
heavy grain on 9:16 reels turns to mush after Instagram compression
slow render on long clips; apply on an adjustment layer once rather than per clip
Intensity above about 2 with Size 3 buries the picture in coarse colour noise (the demo at Intensity 4 is barely legible); keep Intensity 0.3-1.5 and turn Monochromatic on for a believable stock

params.name: Viewing Mode
params.does: dropdown: Preview box, Blending Matte or Final Output

params.name: Preset
params.does: dropdown of film-stock grain presets (1 = none)

params.name: Intensity
params.does: amount of grain

params.name: Size
params.does: grain particle size

params.name: Softness
params.does: blur of the grain particles

params.name: Monochromatic
params.does: checkbox: grey grain without colour noise

params.name: Saturation
params.does: colour saturation of the grain

params.name: Animation Speed
params.does: how fast the grain changes (0 = frozen)

cards.equivalent: Noise (Premiere; plain per-pixel noise, no film-stock, size or softness controls)
cards.scripting: ALWAYS set Viewing Mode = 3 (Final Output); the default 1 (Preview) shows grain only inside the Preview Region box (Center/Width/Height, drawn with Box Color). Preset (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 [None], 2 a separator, 3-15 film stocks from Eastman Color Neg II 100T (5247) to Kodak SFX 200T (enum_labels); a non-1 preset may override the Tweaking values (not rendered). Mask Layer is a layer-reference param (not settable from a spec). Amount (Blend with Original) is 0-100.

verified.note: Coarse multicoloured grain covers the whole frame so heavily (Intensity 4, Size 3, well above the 0.3-1.5 typical) that the figures and stripes are barely legible: unmistakably Add Grain, far past a realistic film look.

cards.name: Dust & Scratches
cards.summary: Median-style filter that replaces pixels differing from their neighbourhood (within Radius) by more than Threshold, removing specks, dust and noise; large radii give a smeared, painterly look.
use_for: clean dust specks and scratches from scanned archival photos in a documentary
light denoise on low-light phone footage
painterly / oil-paint stylisation of a still at high Radius
smooth a noisy matte before choking
avoid: Radius above 3-4 with Threshold 0 smears faces into plastic
on moving footage it can flicker; a real denoiser is better for noise

params.name: Radius
params.does: size of the area searched for differing pixels
params.typical: 1-3 to clean, 8-20 for a painterly look

params.name: Threshold
params.does: how different a pixel must be to be replaced (0 = all pixels)

params.name: Operate on Alpha channel
params.does: checkbox: also filters the alpha

cards.equivalent: none in Premiere 2026 (its effect list has neither Dust & Scratches nor Median); do the cleanup in AE
cards.scripting: The harvest reports Threshold as 0-1, while the AE panel is documented as 0-255; values above 1 are clamped. Whether 1 here means panel 255 (so convert UI/255) or panel 1 is unverified: read the value back in the panel after setting it. Render time grows quickly with Radius. For real noise on moving footage use Remove Grain instead.

verified.note: Radius 10 at Threshold 0 median-smooths the frame: faces lose features and turn plastic, hair and fine detail smear and fine texture drops (edge energy down about 60%) while big shapes and stripes stay put.
